title: Batch HID lock snapshot in AppState report callback
description: onReportData currently grabs OSAllocatedUnfairLock repeatedly via cachedIsLeftController, cachedIsEnabled, cachedJoystickScrollEnabled/Speed/Acceleration, and trigger threshold. Acquire the lock once, capture all needed cached values (plus pause flag if feasible), and use that snapshot for the entire HID report processing path. Goal: minimize per-report lock/unlock churn on the ~60–66 Hz hot path without changing behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- onReportData performs at most one lock acquisition for cached values per report (excluding unavoidable pause check) and uses a snapshot for subsequent logic
- Gyro, joystick scroll, and button processing behave identically (no regression in modes or enable/disable behavior)
- Measured or reasoned lock/unlock count per report is reduced vs current implementation

title: Swap NSLock to OSAllocatedUnfairLock in hot paths
description: AppState uses NSLock for cached flags accessed from HID callbacks. Replace with OSAllocatedUnfairLock (or os_unfair_lock) for lower overhead and to match GyroSettings’ locking approach. Keep the API surface the same while reducing lock latency on the input thread.

title: Make settings tabs type-aware (Controller, Buttons, Mouse/Stick) for Joy-Con
description: Update Controller/Buttons/Mouse/Stick tabs to switch content based on controller type: Joy-Con gets its own button list (including the extra four buttons) and stick controls; PSVR2 keeps its current UI. Ensure the tabs read/write the correct stored profile per type and show a Joy-Con-specific selector in the Controller tab. For now, focus on UI/plumbing, not full action execution.

title: Reuse debug buffers to reduce allocations when debug is on
description: When debug rendering is active, reuse preallocated buffers/arrays for pending byte/bit changes and report copies instead of rebuilding them each report. Clear by count instead of reallocating to keep the HID path lean even while debugging.

comments.author: jturnshek
comments.text: Closed in error; debug buffer reuse not implemented yet.

title: Add controller-type aware selection and persistence
description: Extend controller discovery/selection to handle both PSVR2 and Joy-Con: unify ControllerInfo with type/side, maintain separate last-selected IDs per type, and allow selecting a single Joy-Con as the active device (PSVR2 can still be selected). Ensure connection change callbacks and AppState track the active controller type for downstream UI/state.

title: Retune One Euro filter and dt handling for 200Hz Joy-Con gyro feed
description: Joy-Con delivers ~200Hz bundled gyro samples but InputProcessor assumes ~66Hz: fallbackRate is forced to 66Hz and expectedDt is 1/66s. This makes the One Euro filter overly aggressive and stall detection too lax. Update the hot path to use a ~200Hz cadence (fallbackRate ~= 200, expectedDt ~= 1/200, matching stall reset threshold) and adjust default minCutoff/beta so the smoothing feel matches PSVR2 at its 60Hz rate. Ensure filter reset still occurs on true stalls and no lag is introduced during fast motion.
acceptance_criteria:
- OneEuroFilter fallbackRate uses the actual ~200Hz Joy-Con cadence; expectedDt in processGyro reflects 1/200s with an appropriate stall clamp
- Default filter settings are retuned for 200Hz so perceived smoothing/latency matches PSVR2 behavior (no added lag compared to current PSVR2 feel)
- Bluetooth stalls still reset the filters correctly; no regressions in cursor stability at rest or during fast flicks

title: Extend Debug tab to display Joy-Con reports/bytes
description: Adapt DebugTab to handle Joy-Con: switch report length/offset metadata based on active controller type, render the byte grid with change highlighting for Joy-Con report length, and surface minimal Joy-Con button/stick/IMU readouts. Keep PSVR2 debug behavior unchanged when PSVR2 is active.

title: Instrument HID→CGEvent latency for Joy-Con gyro path
description: We need hard numbers on where latency accrues. Add optional diagnostics that timestamp at key points: (1) IOHIDValue callback arrival, (2) after decoding, (3) before/after processGyro, (4) before CGEvent post. Emit lightweight logs/counters (guarded behind a debug flag) so we can measure average/max latency and stalls without spamming production builds.
acceptance_criteria:
- Debug mode captures timestamps at HID callback, post-decode, pre/post processGyro, and pre-CGEvent post, computing deltas without significant overhead when enabled
- Diagnostics are gated (off by default) and safe to leave in production builds
- Documentation or log output shows how to enable and collect the latency measurements, and demonstrates end-to-end timing with Joy-Con

title: Reduce Date() calls in radial menu trail update
description: Pass a single timestamp through radial menu trail update/pruning to avoid multiple Date() allocations per gyro update when radial menu is active.

title: Strengthen dt fallback and diagnostics
description: Keep using device timestamps, but add guards for nil/duplicate device ts (fallback to host time) and log/diagnose when dt hits clamp thresholds frequently. Aim is to make jitter handling more robust and observable without changing core behavior.

title: Cache gyro settings snapshot for HID hot path
description: Avoid per-report OSAllocatedUnfairLock read of gyroSettings in AppState.onReportData by maintaining a cached settings snapshot updated on change, so HID processing uses a lock-free struct (similar to other cached values).

title: Debounce disk writes for sliders (gyro, radial, mappings) to remove laggy drags
description:
Observed: slider didSets call persistence on every tick (e.g., `gyroSettings.save()` inside AppState gyro properties; `UserDefaults` writes in joystick/radial sliders; radial menu config JSON saved on every change). Dragging sliders drives synchronous disk I/O on the main thread, contributing to UI stutter.
Proposal:
- Switch sliders to update in-memory state during drag and persist on `onEditingChanged == false` or via a short debounce (e.g., DispatchWorkItem) on the main queue.
- Keep live values for processing, but batch writes to `UserDefaults`/JSON to avoid per-tick file churn.
Files: Sources/PSVR2Gyro/AppState.swift (gyro @Published didSets, joystick scroll settings); Sources/PSVR2Gyro/Models/GyroSettings.swift (save); Sources/PSVR2Gyro/Models/RadialMenu.swift (save); Sources/PSVR2Gyro/Views/Settings/*.swift (sliders).
Goal: Slider drags feel responsive with no visible hitch from synchronous persistence.

title: Implement Joy-Con raw HID driver (PSVR2-style)
description: Add a Nintendo Joy-Con HID driver that mirrors PSVR2Controller: match vendor 0x057E and PIDs 0x2006/0x2007, probe type via SPI 0x6012, send subcommands to set input mode 0x30 and enable IMU, seize device, and stream raw input reports (define JoyConHIDProtocol with report length/offsets). Expose callbacks for report bytes + decoded gyro/accel, stick, and battery, using a reusable buffer and Mach timestamps similar to PSVR2.

title: Track cursor internally with periodic resync to reduce per-move mouseLocation calls
description: Maintain an internal cursor position in Cocoa coordinates and apply gyro dx/dy to it, posting CGEvents without calling NSEvent.mouseLocation every move. Resync from the system cursor on startup, screen changes, after drags/warps, or on a low-rate timer to handle external cursor moves. Ensure clamping stays correct and coordinate spaces remain consistent. Goal: remove per-move mouseLocation lookup while keeping cursor behavior stable.

title: Coalesce radial menu updates to avoid per-report Task creation
description: When gyro mode is .radialMenu, onReportData spawns a new Task {@MainActor} for every HID report, which can queue up if the main actor lags. Introduce coalescing (e.g., store latest delta and drive a single main-actor updater) to keep UI current without spawning one task per sample.
acceptance_criteria:
- Radial menu gyro updates no longer create an unbounded Task per report; updates are coalesced or limited to one in-flight
- UI responsiveness for radial selection remains correct (no dropped highlights/selection errors)
- No accumulation of pending Tasks on the main actor under load

title: Run HID manager on dedicated high-QoS run loop
description: Currently IOHIDManager is scheduled on the main CFRunLoop (see PSVR2Controller.start), so SwiftUI/UI work can delay HID report handling, inflating dt and adding jitter. Move HID scheduling to a dedicated high-priority thread/run loop for input processing and only dispatch UI updates back to the main actor. This should reduce latency spikes and stutter in gyro-driven mouse movement.

title: Use real HID timestamps for bundled Joy-Con samples instead of clamped spacing
description: JoyConSwift backfills per-sample timestamps by dividing the packet delta by 3 and clamping spacing to 1/200–1/2000s. If a packet is late, downstream code still thinks samples were spaced 5ms apart, masking stalls and skewing dt. Relax or remove the clamp and propagate the true Mach-based timestamps so InputProcessor can see real gaps and reset filters appropriately.
acceptance_criteria:
- Per-sample timestamps reflect actual Mach ticks (no fixed 5ms clamp when packets are late); sample spacing is derived from real packet deltas
- InputProcessor receives monotonic timestamps that never go backward and handles stalls correctly (filters reset on real gaps)
- No regressions in gyro processing stability; dt remains within a sensible bound to avoid divide-by-small errors

title: Gate debug byte/bit tracking and reuse report buffers
description: Per-report debug bookkeeping runs even when not viewing the debug tab: full 78-byte copies, byte/bit change tracking, and Date allocations. Add a flag to skip this work when debug rendering is off and reuse preallocated buffers to reduce allocations and comparisons on the HID thread.

title: Deburst bundled Joy-Con samples so CGEvents aren’t posted in 66Hz bursts
description: Each Joy-Con HID packet contains 3 gyro samples but sensorHandler fires them back-to-back, so mouse moves post in 66Hz bursts rather than ~200Hz spacing. Evaluate and implement a low-latency strategy: either process only the newest sample per packet (for latency parity with PSVR2) or spread the 3 samples over ~5ms intervals without adding noticeable lag. Goal: smoother, more responsive cursor updates instead of clumped bursts.
acceptance_criteria:
- Hot path no longer posts all three sample deltas at once each packet; either single-sample or time-sliced delivery is implemented and selectable if needed
- End-user cursor motion feels smoother (no bursty micro-stutter) and latency does not increase relative to current behavior
- No regression in clutch/scroll/zoom modes; sampling strategy applies consistently across modes

title: Reduce Joy-Con gyro hot-path overhead (raw Int16 + single settings snapshot)
description: On each gyro sample we allocate GyroData, convert Float→Double, and read many InputSettings fields individually (multiple lock hits). Introduce a raw Int16 + timestamp path from JoyConSwift into InputProcessor (matching PSVR2), and add a single InputSettings snapshot for gyro processing to cut per-sample locking. Objective: lower CPU/latency on the HID thread without changing behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- Gyro processing can consume raw Int16 values + timestamp directly (or uses a zero-allocation struct) without Float→Double conversions on the hot path
- InputProcessor receives a single settings snapshot per gyro dispatch instead of multiple lock acquisitions
- Behavior (sensitivity, mapping, filtering) matches current output; no regressions in clutch/scroll/zoom or activity detection

title: Apply button/mode state before gyro movement per report
description: Currently onGyroData runs before onReportData updates button states and gyro mode, so drag/scroll/clutch toggles apply one packet late. Reorder processing so button/joystick decoding and mode selection happen for the same HID report before applying gyro deltas, eliminating a frame of latency when switching modes.

title: Reuse HID report buffer and avoid double gyro/accel decoding
description: handleInputReport allocates a new [UInt8] per report and decodes gyro/accel, then AppState decodes gyro/accel again. Reuse a persistent buffer (or pointer) for the report bytes, and pass the already-decoded IMU values/timestamp to AppState to eliminate the extra allocation and double decode.
acceptance_criteria:
- No per-report heap allocation for the 78-byte input report (buffer is reused)
- AppState consumes pre-decoded gyro/accel/timestamp without re-decoding the same bytes
- IMU/gyro processing and debug views still receive correct data

title: Reduce radial menu trail allocations and tighten angle normalization
description: TrailPoint currently allocates a UUID and Date per point, and angle normalization uses while loops. Replace UUID with a lightweight incrementing ID, reuse a single timestamp per update, keep trail capacity between updates, and switch angle normalization to fmod-based clamping. Preserve visual behavior and lifetime limits.
acceptance_criteria:
- Trail point creation avoids UUID() and reuses a timestamp per update; removeAll uses keepingCapacity where appropriate
- Angle normalization uses fmod (or equivalent bounded math) instead of unbounded while loops
- Radial menu trail visuals and selection behavior remain unchanged (maxTrailPoints and lifetime respected)

title: Optimize radial menu rendering (static layers + lightweight cursor/highlight)
description:
Observed: `RadialMenuState` publishes `ghostPosition`/highlight indexes and `RadialMenuView` rebuilds all pie slices, labels, glass effects every cursor move. Trig/layout runs per-frame, and highlight changes force full view recomposition.
Proposal:
- Split static geometry (inner/outer ring slices + labels) into a pre-rendered layer/Canvas or an `EquatableView` keyed by `RadialMenuConfiguration`, and keep a minimal overlay for ghost cursor/highlight.
- Reduce per-delta main-thread churn: replace per-report `Task { @MainActor ... }` in `AppState` radial path with a throttled main queue hop or dedicated actor; consider trimming trail computations to avoid new Dates in the view.
Files: Sources/PSVR2Gyro/Views/RadialMenuView.swift; Sources/PSVR2Gyro/Models/RadialMenuState.swift; Sources/PSVR2Gyro/AppState.swift (radial menu update scheduling).
Goal: Radial menu and ghost cursor stay smooth at 60–120 Hz without re-rendering all slices on each move.

title: Trim per-report allocations in AppState hot path
description: Minor hot-path cleanups: reuse/cached PSVR2ButtonMapping for left/right, avoid creating the byteAt closure per report, and only call Date()/debug tracking when debug rendering is active.
acceptance_criteria:
- No per-report allocation of PSVR2ButtonMapping or byteAt closure in onReportData
- Date() and debug tracking work are skipped entirely when debug rendering is disabled
- Functional behavior for mapping, debug bytes/bits, and UI updates remains unchanged

title: Hook Joy-Con reports into AppState and type-specific storage
description: Wire the new Joy-Con driver into AppState: route onReportData/onConnectionChange into existing throttling, resize report buffers to Joy-Con length when active, and add a Joy-Con-specific button mapping profile + settings store (shared across Joy-Cons) without affecting PSVR2 profiles. Maintain type-aware cached values so downstream processing can branch without crashes when the report length/offsets differ.

title: Replace button state dictionaries with fixed-size storage on HID path
description: processButtonActions and buttonStates use Dictionary<LogicalButton,Bool> and look up mappings via string keys, adding hashing overhead each report. Replace with array/bitset keyed by an integer-backed enum to remove per-frame dictionary costs while preserving semantics (press/release edge detection, holds, and exported buttonStates for UI/debug).
acceptance_criteria:
- Button state tracking on the HID thread no longer uses Dictionary lookups per button
- Edge detection, hold timers, and buttonStates exposure still function correctly
- LogicalButton can be indexed deterministically (e.g., stable ordering) to back the fixed-size storage

title: Use circular buffer for gyro bias samples
description: GyroProcessor.updateBias appends samples and trims with removeFirst(), adding O(n) churn in the bias buffer. Replace with a fixed-size ring buffer to keep bias updates O(1) and avoid allocations while collecting stationary samples.

title: GyroProcessor math/alloc optimizations and OneEuro constant
description: Tighten GyroProcessor hot path: preallocate bias buffer up front, maintain running sums to avoid per-sample reduce, reuse a single speed/sqrt result across acceleration/adaptive beta, and hoist 2π to a static constant in OneEuroFilter. Also skip gyro/accel decoding when callbacks are nil to avoid wasted work.
acceptance_criteria:
- Bias buffer is allocated once (not lazily on first stationary frame) and bias updates avoid O(n) reduce per sample by using a running sum/count
- Speed computation reused (no redundant sqrt) in adaptive smoothing/acceleration
- OneEuroFilter uses a cached 2π constant instead of recomputing each call
- Gyro/accel decoding in PSVR2Controller is skipped when corresponding callbacks are nil
- No behavior regressions in calibration, filtering, or cursor feel

title: Simplify joystick scroll math and gating
description: Trim per-report math in joystick scroll: consider a lighter-weight acceleration or power curve, and ensure the path is fully gated when not in use. Goal: reduce computation on the HID thread for joystick scroll users while keeping feel acceptable.

title: Cache drag/scroll/radial mapping flags instead of per-frame scans
description: currentGyroMode calls buttonMappingProfile.hasDragMapping (and similar) which scans the mappings dictionary each frame on the HID hot path. Cache booleans for hasDragMapping/hasScrollMapping/hasRadialMenuMapping whenever the profile is loaded or mutated, and use those cached values in currentGyroMode.
acceptance_criteria:
- hasDragMapping/hasScrollMapping/hasRadialMenuMapping are computed when the mapping profile changes, not each frame
- currentGyroMode uses cached flags and performs no dictionary scan on the hot path
- Behavior remains identical for mode selection when mappings are edited

title: Use device/driver timestamps for gyro dt
description: Gyro processing uses host arrival time (CACurrentMediaTime) from IOHIDDeviceRegisterInputReportCallback. Switch to an input value callback that exposes IOHIDValueGetTimeStamp (or otherwise decode a monotonic counter if present) so dt is based on device/driver time rather than run-loop jitter. Add dt clamping/high-gap reset logic to keep One Euro filter and acceleration stable.

title: Throttle debug publishes to avoid UI jank in settings tabs
description:
Observed: `AppState` publishes `lastGyro*`, `lastAccel*`, `reportCount`, `batteryLevel`, `debugRefreshTrigger`, etc. every ~30–60 fps from `setupReportCallback`, while all tabs observe the same `AppState`, causing TabView/ScrollView recomputation and sluggish scrolling/slider drags even when not on the Debug tab.
Proposal:
- Gate or move live telemetry (`lastGyro*`, `lastAccel*`, `reportCount`, `batteryLevel`, `debugRefreshTrigger`) behind the Debug tab (`activeTab == .debug && debugRenderingEnabled`) or isolate into a debug-only observable model.
- Keep connection/meta fields publishing, but stop frame-ticker publishes from invalidating non-debug UI.
Files: Sources/PSVR2Gyro/AppState.swift (setupReportCallback, published properties); Sources/PSVR2Gyro/Views/Settings/*.swift (Tabs/TabHeader observe AppState).
Goal: scrolling and slider drags in settings are smooth because they no longer get rebuilt at 30+ fps by debug telemetry.
notes: Started implementation to gate debug publishes and throttle battery updates to reduce UI churn.

title: Cache ButtonActions by LogicalButton index to avoid string hashing
description: Maintain an array of ButtonActions keyed by LogicalButton.index to eliminate per-event String dictionary lookups in button action processing; update the cache whenever the mapping profile changes.

title: Cache screen bounds and cursor lookup off the hot path
description: MouseController recalculates NSScreen.screens, unions bounds, and queries NSEvent.mouseLocation on every move. Cache screen geometry and cursor position using CGDisplay APIs, update on screen-change notifications, and keep the movement path free of AppKit calls to reduce stutter.

title: Stop re-instantiating radial menu preview state on tab recompute
description:
Observed: `RadialMenuTab` constructs a new `RadialMenuState` in `previewState` every body recompute. Because the tab observes `AppState`, unrelated publishes (e.g., connection or settings changes) rebuild the preview `RadialMenuView`, causing needless allocations and render work.
Proposal:
- Hold a `@StateObject`/cached preview state that only updates when `radialMenuConfiguration` changes, or derive a simple `View` that doesn’t recreate the state per recomposition.
Files: Sources/PSVR2Gyro/Views/Settings/RadialMenuTab.swift (menuPreview/previewState).
Goal: Radial tab stays responsive; preview does not churn when unrelated app state changes.
